title: Send an invoice
summary: Create and send an invoice to a customer for services rendered. Stripe is the canonical route; any payments provider with invoicing works.

parts.title: Look up or create customer
parts.guidance: Find the customer’s existing billing record from the contract or order before creating another. Check legal name, address, relevant tax identifiers, currency, purchase-order requirements and billing contact. Resolve conflicts with the account owner or customer through the established channel, leaving a billing record that matches the agreed commercial relationship.

execution.rationale: Stripe customer listing supports the existing-record check, and customer creation records the verified billing details when no matching customer exists.

parts.title: Create invoice with line items
parts.guidance: Draft the invoice from the contract or order and the billable milestone or service period. Check quantities, prices, discounts, currency, payment terms and tax treatment, using the applicable local invoice route. Recalculate totals and compare earlier invoices to avoid duplicate billing. Resolve exceptions with the billing owner before the document is issued.

options.title: Default — Create invoice with line items
options.summary: Describe line items so the customer can recognize what was delivered and when. Match quantities, prices, discounts and service periods to the order, with the correct tax treatment, payment terms and purchase-order reference. Check the total and any departure from agreed terms so the draft is ready for the billing owner to issue.

execution.rationale: Stripe's invoice and invoice-item APIs support the reviewed line items and terms as a draft invoice.

options.title: India - GST e-invoice (IRN)
options.summary: Establish GST treatment and e-invoicing applicability with the Indian tax owner for this supplier and document. Where an IRN is required, the authorized billing user submits accurate seller, buyer, supply and amount data through an eligible route. Match the returned IRN, signed data and QR information to the invoice and resolve validation errors before delivery.

execution.rationale: The authorized billing operator submits the invoice through the selected e-invoice service and checks the returned IRN, signed data and QR information.

options.title: UK - statutory VAT invoice
options.summary: For the UK invoice, check party details, unique number, supply and issue dates, descriptions, charges and total against the transaction. Determine whether a VAT invoice is required and apply its fields and treatment. Use the agreed payment terms, resolving any proposed late-payment charge before the billing owner issues the final document.

execution.rationale: Prepare the UK invoice from supplied transaction facts and the tax owner's settled treatment for issuance review.

options.title: Germany - s.14 UStG e-invoice
options.summary: Establish the German invoice particulars, VAT treatment and electronic format required for the parties and transaction. Populate the invoice from the contract and delivery evidence, checking identifiers, dates and amounts. Validate structured output where required alongside its readable presentation, then issue it through the billing owner’s accounting workflow.

execution.rationale: The billing operator prepares and validates the required digital invoice format and issues it through the supported customer delivery channel.

options.title: France - mentions obligatoires
options.summary: Check the French invoice’s party identities, transaction details, price, tax presentation and applicable payment statements against current requirements. Establish the electronic-invoicing channel and obligations for the company’s size and transaction with the accountant. Validate the document or structured submission, then follow platform acknowledgments or correction requests against the issued invoice.

execution.rationale: The billing operator uses the applicable digital invoicing platform and checks required invoice content, acknowledgements and correction handling.

parts.title: Send invoice
parts.guidance: The billing owner sends the final invoice to the verified contact or required customer portal with the correct attachments, purchase-order reference and payment instructions. Check the delivery acknowledgment and resolve rejected or failed submissions. Link corrections and re-delivery to the original invoice to preserve a single receivable for the charge.

execution.rationale: The billing operator delivers the invoice and required attachments through the customer-facing billing interface and verifies the delivery status.

parts.title: Track payment status
parts.guidance: Match receipts to the invoice by customer, reference, amount and currency, accounting for partial payments, credits and fees. Keep unpaid, disputed and settled balances distinct. Investigate mismatches and follow the agreed collection process for overdue amounts, using the account owner’s customer context to resolve disputes or arrange the next action.

execution.rationale: Stripe's invoice dashboard exposes paid, open and past-due balances and customer details for reconciliation and collection follow-up.

geoNotes.summary: Invoices are GST documents: registered businesses past ₹5 crore turnover must clear every B2B invoice through the government IRP (e-invoicing) to get an IRN and QR code — an invoice without one simply isn't valid.

Invoices must carry the statutory particulars (and full VAT-invoice fields once registered); late payers owe statutory interest at 8% over base under the late-payment legislation — gov.uk documents both.

§ 14 UStG fixes the mandatory invoice fields (sequential number, Steuernummer/USt-IdNr, …) — and since January 2025 every German business must be able to RECEIVE structured e-invoices (XRechnung/ZUGFeRD) for domestic B2B, with issuing phasing in.

French invoices carry a long list of mentions obligatoires (SIREN, RCS, per-line detail, late-payment penalty terms…), and mandatory B2B e-invoicing via accredited platforms (PDP) phases in from September 2026 — receiving first, issuing by 2027.

Once GST-registered, invoices must be proper tax invoices with the prescribed particulars — and GST-registered businesses are being phased onto InvoiceNow (Peppol) e-invoicing, so pick software that speaks it.
B2B invoicing runs on the electronic tax invoice (전자세금계산서) issued through Hometax, which doubles as the VAT paper trail.

Invoices carry no tax line: Hong Kong has no sales tax, GST or VAT, so an invoice is a commercial document rather than a tax artifact — keep the business records the Inland Revenue Ordinance requires for 7 years and pick software accordingly.

Invoices follow the Accounting Act's source-document rules, and since July 2025 a buyer registered as an e-invoice recipient in the commercial register can require a machine-readable e-invoice to the European standard (Accounting Act § 7¹).

metadata.supportReason: Stripe Invoicing API fully supports create, send, and track.
